solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dynamism versus current inanity, leaving university (8)

indicators.note: to leave is to walk out, so the university's letter walks out of the word

blocks.note: v = versus, as in a fixture list
I is the physics symbol for electric current
VACUITY (inanity) without U (university)

annotation.surface: A debate pitting energy against the empty-headedness of the moment, with academia bowing out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' qualifying inanity; in crosswords it is usually I, the symbol for electric current.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: dynamism and vivacity both describe a lively, energetic manner.

entries.clue: Confirm uncertainty really is inhibiting (6)

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold something in check, so VERY holds IF inside it

blocks.note: really = very, as in 'really good'
an if is a doubt, as in 'no ifs or buts'

annotation.surface: Someone admitting that doubt is holding back the confirmation everyone wants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncertainty' reads as a feeling holding someone back; it is a noun meaning a doubt, a word that crosswords often shrink to two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to establish that something is true.

entries.clue: Half in vain, perhaps Ulysses is a wanderer (7)

indicators.note: take half of the word 'vain': its first two letters

blocks.note: the first half of VAIN
Ulysses S. Grant, US general and president; 'perhaps' flags him as one Ulysses among others

annotation.surface: A literary remark that Homer's or Joyce's Ulysses is, at least half the time, a wanderer.
annotation.walkthrough: Ulysses wants to be the wandering Greek hero, which fits 'wanderer' perfectly; here it is the American president Ulysses S. Grant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person with no settled home who drifts from place to place.

entries.clue: Fish take food almost on top of pond? Nonsense (10)

indicators.note: almost is nearly all, so the word stops short of its last letter
the top of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, a piece that is on another sits above it

blocks.note: the cod, a common food fish
SWALLOW (take food) without its final W
first letter of POND

annotation.surface: Fish rising to feed at the surface of a pond, followed by a scornful dismissal.
annotation.walkthrough: The pond scene tempts you to read 'top of pond' as the water's surface; it is only its first letter. Codswallop is British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British informal slang for rubbish talk.

entries.clue: Fund-raising preacher tells eg native to convert (13)

indicators.note: converting changes one thing into another, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A preacher raising money who tells, for instance, a local person that they must convert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convert' fits the preacher's mission so well that it reads as religious conversion, not as a signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a preacher on television, famous for appealing to viewers for donations.

entries.clue: Diver almost out of breath (6)

indicators.note: almost is nearly all, so the word stops one letter short of the end

blocks.note: PUFFING (out of breath) without its final G

annotation.surface: A diver surfacing nearly winded.
annotation.walkthrough: The diver is a person in the surface but a bird in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this seabird dives from the surface to catch fish.

entries.clue: One of fifty in uniform tipped cap? (4)

indicators.note: tipped over, so in a down clue the word is turned upside down

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a cap is a kind of hat

annotation.surface: A soldier among fifty in uniform, tipping their cap in salute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tipped cap' reads as a polite salute; here the cap is tipped over, upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one member of the set of fifty US states.

entries.clue: Football manager with one draw and a defeat (7)

blocks.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English football
I is the Roman numeral one
to draw someone in is to lure them

annotation.surface: A football manager whose season brings one draw and a loss.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'draw' a tied match; here it is a verb, to attract. The manager is not a person but English football's governing body.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a loss, the opposite of success.

entries.clue: No German announced links for ten years (8)

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the German word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: nein is German for no, and sounds like the number after eight
ties are links or bonds

annotation.surface: A German official refusing to announce a decade-long partnership.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Links' could be golf courses, but here they are bonds.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a decade such as 1990 to 1999 spans ten years.

entries.clue: Scrap paper (3)

blocks.note: a scrap of cloth
a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper

annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap paper' reads as a single thing; split it into two words that each give the answer. Rag is a British sneer at a tabloid newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a torn scrap of cloth, and a scornful word for a cheap newspaper.

entries.clue: Act of removing constant cheers interrupts enjoyment (11)

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the letters go into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: deletion is the act of removing
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
ta is British informal for thanks

annotation.surface: Someone who keeps shouting approval and spoils another's fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like applause or a toast; in British English it also means thanks, and so does ta.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean great pleasure, delectation being the more formal word.

entries.clue: Getting better clubs, deceptively conceal seven (13)

indicators.note: the letters are presented in a misleading order

blocks.note: C is clubs, the card suit
anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A golfer improving their game by cheating to hide an extra seven clubs in the bag.
annotation.walkthrough: The golfing surface makes clubs a bag of irons; here clubs is only the card suit, and joins the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: 'getting better' as a gerund names the period of recovery after illness.

entries.clue: Tire, indicating one’s leaving patriotic display (4-6)

blocks.note: to flag is to tire
you wave goodbye when you leave

annotation.surface: Someone growing tired and signalling it is time to go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tire' looks like a noun (the American spelling of tyre); it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: literally waving the national flag, and by extension any showy patriotism.

entries.clue: Barely succeeded in project (4)

indicators.note: 'in' places S inside the other word, as a person is in a room

blocks.note: to jut is to project, stick out
s. = succeeded, as in family trees and lists of monarchs

annotation.surface: A project that squeaked through as a success by a whisker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun, a scheme; it is the verb, to stick out. S for succeeded is a genealogy abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiomatic sense: 'just made it' means barely made it.

entries.clue: Wine box in bedroom? (10)

blocks.note: chamber is an old word for a bedroom
a tin is a box

annotation.surface: A case of wine kept in the bedroom.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a play on words: a box that lives in the bedroom would be a bedroom box, and the words run in that order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin.

entries.clue: War leader large, in colour (6)

indicators.note: 'in colour' says L sits inside the word for colour, as paint sits in a tin

blocks.note: a stain colours wood or cloth
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A wartime commander painted large and in full colour, like a propaganda poster.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a propaganda poster, larger than life; the colour is a wood dye.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Soviet dictator led his country through the Second World War.

entries.clue: One allowed into cycling eliminator? (7)

indicators.note: 'into' sends one word inside another
the letters go round in a cycle, the first moving to the end

blocks.note: HEAT, a qualifying round, with its first letter cycled to the end
let = allowed

annotation.surface: A rider admitted to a qualifying race in a cycling event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like the sport; here it tells you to move letters round in a ring. Read straight, the whole clue also describes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: a competitor admitted to a qualifying heat is exactly what the clue describes.

entries.clue: Released, travelled quite a distance in the van (8)

indicators.note: the van is the front of an army, so the letter at the front of 'distance'

blocks.note: ran = travelled, as a bus runs
'that's some car' means quite a car
first letter of DISTANCE

annotation.surface: A freed hostage driven a long way in the back of a van.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle; it is short for vanguard, the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrower sense: freed from captivity on payment of a ransom.

entries.clue: Turn out chasing a parking permit (7)

indicators.note: a chaser runs behind, so this piece comes after the others

blocks.note: as printed
P is the parking sign
to turn out, as in 'it proved true'

annotation.surface: A traffic warden turning out to chase a driver over a parking permit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parking permit' reads as one thing; 'permit' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as verbs, both mean to allow.

entries.clue: He painted a little chicken (7)

definitions.note: 'He painted' stands for 'he who painted', the painter

blocks.note: Nicolas, the French classical painter of the 1600s
the French word for a young chicken, used on British menus

annotation.surface: An artist dabbling with a small painting of a chick.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'He painted a little' together and you picture an amateur. Split it: the painter, and the young bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the surname of a French painter, and a chicken killed young for eating.

entries.clue: Determined where this carnivore lurks (6)

indicators.note: points to the word the answer sits in
to lurk is to hide, so the answer hides inside 'Determined'

blocks.note: the six letters between the outer Ds

annotation.surface: A resolute stoat lying in wait.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a statement about a determined hunter; in fact 'Determined' is where the animal hides.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the stoat, especially in its white winter coat, is a small meat-eater.

entries.clue: Foreign wood carving wins British prize at last (7)

indicators.note: at the end, so take the final letter of 'prize'

blocks.note: to net is to win or gain
UK, the United Kingdom
last letter of PRIZE

annotation.surface: An imported wooden sculpture taking a British award.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' is fair because the carving is Japanese: a small toggle, often of wood or ivory.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small Japanese carved toggle, often wooden.

entries.clue: Drinks all day then falls down (6)

blocks.note: d = day
rain falls down

annotation.surface: A drunk who drinks all day and then keels over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falls down' looks like a drunk collapsing; it is weather. The definition is 'Drinks all', not 'Drinks'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to drain a glass is to empty it by drinking.

entries.clue: Shock, almost attacked by bee (4)

indicators.note: almost is nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: STUNG (attacked by a bee) without its final G

annotation.surface: The shock of nearly being stung.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost' here trims a word, not the attack: the bee's sting is complete, only its final letter goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to daze with a sudden blow or surprise.

entries.clue: When it snows perhaps burying revolutionary’s rifle (10)

indicators.note: to bury is to put inside, so the outer word surrounds the revolutionary

blocks.note: winter is when it may snow
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, plus 's

annotation.surface: A guerrilla hiding his gun in the snow.
annotation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary; 'perhaps' warns that snow is only one example of the season's weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lever-action repeating gun is the classic rifle of the Wild West.

entries.clue: Fine internet address: roll up! (4)

blocks.note: f = fine, on pencil grades
a URL is a web address

annotation.surface: A showman's shout advertising a fine website: roll up, roll up!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roll up!' looks like a fairground barker's call; it is the definition, as you would a flag or sail.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to roll up a sail, flag or umbrella and fasten it.

entries.clue: Doctor’s left a person with temperature a shield against infection (8,3)

blocks.note: MO (medical officer, a doctor) plus 's
quit = left, departed
one = a person, as in 'one never knows'
T = temperature

annotation.surface: A doctor walking out on a feverish patient who needed protecting from infection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the side; it is the verb, departed. The shield works against malaria, carried by the insects it keeps out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the mesh keeps off malaria-carrying insects, shielding the sleeper from infection.

entries.clue: One student finally leaves here? (3)

indicators.note: at the end, so the last letter of 'student'
to leave is to go away, so that letter departs from the word for one

blocks.note: a unit is one
T, the last letter of STUDENT, goes out of UNIT

annotation.surface: A student at last leaving after graduation.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition 'here' refers to the whole clue: the place a student eventually leaves, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by reference: 'here' is the place the clue describes, the university a student finally leaves.

entries.clue: Temptingly hold out diamonds with devious motive (6)

blocks.note: D is diamonds, the card suit
an angle is a scheme or ulterior motive

annotation.surface: A con man offering diamonds as bait, with an ulterior motive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' looks like jewels; it is the card suit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: dangling a carrot is holding out a temptation.

entries.clue: Shabby state of girl in disorder (8)

indicators.note: 'in disorder' puts the girl inside the word for disorder, as someone is in a mess

blocks.note: a mess is disorder
a girl's name

annotation.surface: A girl living in a shabby, untidy state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Girl' in crosswords is often just any short female name; here the one that fits has four letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: meanness can mean shabbiness or poverty of appearance, not only stinginess.
